azure.why: Read-only Azure tools through az login; each pack picks its namespaces (no Key Vault). App Service settings, which can hold connection strings, are returned only after a consent prompt. The foundry and arm namespaces proxy Microsoft's hosted servers, so which of their tools count as read-only comes from those services at run time, and foundryextensions can call deployed models, which spends tokens. The first start downloads about 62 MB.

docs-langchain.why: Searches the LangChain, LangGraph and Deep Agents docs, current to the release, instead of what a model remembers.

fastmcp-docs.why: Searches the FastMCP docs (two read-only tools); its feedback tool is denied.

figma.why: Figma's own remote server, read-only: design context and code for a linked frame, variables, screenshots, outlines, library search and Code Connect maps. Each person signs in to Figma in the client (/mcp in Claude Code, codex mcp login figma); nothing is stored, and a personal access token can't sign it in. Its write tools are denied here and offered by figma-write; Weave's run tools are denied everywhere. Codex gets only the read tools Figma documents. A Dev or Full seat gets 200 calls a day on Professional; View and Collab seats get 20 a month.

figma-write.why: Optional: the same Figma server with its write tools: use_figma builds and edits frames, components and variables through the Plugin API; others turn web UI or HTML into layers, create files, upload assets, generate images, and save Code Connect mappings. It reaches a repository with the figma pack only on a machine granted it (globals --allow-write-mcp figma-write), in that checkout's Claude Code local scope and ignored Codex file, and Claude Code asks before every write. Sign in to it separately. Figma needs edit access to the file, and a Dev seat writes only to drafts; write in the Sandbox folder, since writing is in beta.

github.why: GitHub-hosted read-only repository, issue and pull-request tools for both clients. Authentication references a machine-owned GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN; no token value is stored. Replaces the Claude GitHub plugin. The endpoint filters tools; use a least-privilege read-only token as well.

gradio-docs.why: Searches and loads the Gradio docs for the gradio pack.

huggingface.why: Finds and inspects models, datasets and Spaces on the Hub, anonymously (read-only).

microsoft-learn.why: Microsoft and Azure documentation for Codex; Claude Code has it from the microsoft-docs plugin.

playwright.why: Drives a real browser for the playwright pack, with every optional capability (coordinate clicks, PDF, devtools tracing and video, network routing, storage and cookies, test assertions, config). Pinned, with a fresh profile each session (--isolated), headless, and output written outside the repository; replaces the playwright plugin, which runs @latest with a persistent profile. browser_run_code_unsafe stays denied: it runs code in the server's own process.

playwright-unsafe.why: Optional: the playwright pack's server with browser_run_code_unsafe allowed, which runs code in the server's own process, so it can do anything this machine's user can. Only in repositories with the playwright pack, on a machine granted it (globals --allow-write-mcp playwright-unsafe), and only in Claude Code's local scope and the ignored .codex/config.toml, never the committed .mcp.json. Claude Code asks before each call. It runs its own browser beside the playwright server's: browse in it for run-code to see the page.

reference-langchain.why: Looks up LangChain API symbols and their signatures.

shadcn.why: Searches and views items in the project's shadcn registries, and gives the command that adds one (it installs nothing itself).

stagehand.why: This repository's own self-hosted Stagehand server: act, extract and observe, with navigation, snapshots and screenshots, on a headless local Chrome with a fresh profile (or your Chrome over STAGEHAND_CDP_URL), answered by your OpenAI-compatible model (STAGEHAND_MODEL_BASE_URL, STAGEHAND_MODEL). It has no Browserbase code path, and a Chrome it launches can't resolve browserbase.com. The first start installs its locked dependencies.

stagehand-docs.why: Searches and reads the Stagehand docs (two read-only tools); its feedback tool is denied. The docs cover Browserbase features this template doesn't use.

mongodb.why: MongoDB's official server for the mongodb pack, pinned, in --readOnly mode: only its read, connect and metadata tools are registered, so it can list databases, collections, indexes and schemas, run find and aggregate, explain queries and inspect search indexes, and never create, update or delete. The deployment comes from the machine's MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING (or the connect tool); no connection string is stored here, and telemetry is off. Atlas tools appear only when MDB_MCP_API_CLIENT_ID and MDB_MCP_API_CLIENT_SECRET are set on the machine.

azure-write.why: Optional infrastructure-changing Azure and Foundry tools. Activate explicitly on this machine; client approvals remain unchanged.

langsmith.why: Optional authenticated LangSmith workspace integration. Complete OAuth in the client; this template stores no credentials.
